key_insight: A machine learning model trained on early-stage node-negative breast cancer cohorts can predict relapse risk and generalize across independent datasets.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help identify patients who could benefit from chemotherapy while reducing overtreatment in lower-risk patients.
method: Trained and tested models on MSK-IMPACT (n=645) and METABRIC (n=503) cohorts
Compared cross-cohort transfer and combined-cohort five-fold cross-validation
Used survival analysis, SHAP interpretability, and ablation analyses to assess clinical relevance
evidence_signal: The combined-cohort model reached AUC 0.788 ± 0.028 in five-fold cross-validation, with cross-cohort AUCs of 0.741 and 0.714 in the two transfer directions and strong survival associations on METABRIC.
watch_item: Performance may vary by cohort, subtype, and data harmonization quality, so external prospective validation is still needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Cross-cohort generalizability of machine learning models for early-stage node-negative breast cancer relapse prediction
